title: Vanishing of multiplicative pairings from two relative one-dimensional tori
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. An $S$-group scheme is a group object in schemes over $S$, with multiplication, inverse and identity obeying the group identities; it is separated when its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. On $S$-schemes use the fppf topology, whose covering families are jointly surjective flat morphisms locally of finite presentation. Write $\mathbf G_a(T)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ with addition and $\mathbf G_m(T)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)^\times$ with multiplication, for every $S$-scheme $T$. A group sheaf means a group-valued functor with unique gluing of compatible sections for these coverings. A central exact sequence means that its first map identifies its source with the kernel of its second map, the second map is locally surjective for this topology, and the kernel commutes with every local section of the middle sheaf. Let $Z$ be a separated commutative $S$-group scheme. If $b:\mathbf G_m\times_S\mathbf G_m\to Z$ is an $S$-morphism which is multiplicative in each argument, meaning $b(aa',c)=b(a,c)b(a',c)$ and $b(a,cc')=b(a,c)b(a,c')$ for all sections after every base change, then $b(a,c)=1$ for all $a,c$ after every base change.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, proof, printed p.127: vanishing of the bi-additive pairing D x D -> Z using the relatively schematically dense torsion subgroups of Gm. Read online on 2026-10-24; local archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this lemma.

proof.text: First verify local divisibility without any restriction on the characteristic. Over a nonempty affine test scheme $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\to S$, identify $D_A(\mathbf Z)$ with $\mathbf G_{m,U}$: a homomorphism from $A[\mathbf Z]=A[t,t^{-1}]$ is uniquely specified by the unit image of $t$. The basis description in [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group] and the affine-spectrum dictionary give this identification. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality] with $M=\mathbf Z$ and $L=n\mathbf Z$, for $n\geq1$. Identifying $L$ with $\mathbf Z$ by $k\mapsto nk$, its quotient map is $[n]:\mathbf G_{m,U}\to\mathbf G_{m,U}$, since $t\mapsto t^n$. Its fppf sheaf quotient is $D_A(L)$. Apply the local-surjectivity clause of [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] to the pointwise quotient presheaf mapping to $h_{D_A(L)}$; its associated-sheaf map is an isomorphism by the quoted quotient assertion. The target is a sheaf by the representable-descent statements cited below. Hence every unit $c$ on $U$ has an $n$th root on an fppf covering. These are coverings in [def-pc-fppf-site]. By [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc] and the uniqueness assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], equality of two morphisms to $Z$ can be checked on that covering. Affine open covers handle any test scheme; on the empty test scheme there is only one morphism.

proof.text:
For each $n\geq1$ let $\mu_n(T)=\{a\in\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)^\times:a^n=1\}$. Multiplicativity and cancellation in the group $Z(T)$ give $b(1,c)=1$. Given $a\in\mu_n(T)$ and a unit $c$, use step 1 locally to write $c=d^n$. Repeated multiplicativity in the two arguments gives
$$b(a,c)=b(a,d^n)=b(a,d)^n=b(a^n,d)=b(1,d)=1.$$
The equality descends by step 1. Thus $b$ agrees with the identity morphism on $\mu_n\times_S\mathbf G_m$ for every positive $n$, as an equality on all test schemes, including nonreduced ones.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition 4.3.1, proof, printed p.127, paragraph proving the vanishing of the bi-additive pairing; explicit expansion of the root-cover and relative-density arguments.

proof.text: Put $X=\mathbf G_m\times_S\mathbf G_m$ and let $e_X:X\to Z$ be its structure map followed by the identity section. The equalizer $E$ of $b$ and $e_X$ is the pullback of $\Delta_{Z/S}$ along $(b,e_X):X\to Z\times_SZ$. Since $Z$ is $S$-separated, its diagonal is a closed immersion; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] makes $E\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion. View $X$ over its second factor $T=\mathbf G_m$. Over an arbitrary affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq T$ it is $\mathbf G_{m,V}=\operatorname{Spec}R[t,t^{-1}]$, by the same unit-representing calculation as in step 1. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], the restriction of $E$ is cut out by an ideal $I\subseteq R[t,t^{-1}]$. Step 2 says that it contains $\mu_{n,V}$ for every $n\geq1$. This subscheme is $\operatorname{Spec}(R[t,t^{-1}]/(t^n-1))$: its morphisms from affine tests are exactly units with $n$th power $1$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], containment means that every element of $I$ maps to zero in every such quotient.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Proposition 4.3.1, proof, printed p.127, paragraph proving the vanishing of the bi-additive pairing; explicit expansion of the root-cover and relative-density arguments.

proof.text: For $f\in I$, multiply by a power $t^k$ so that $g=t^kf\in R[t]$. Choose $n\geq1$ strictly larger than every exponent appearing in $g$. The quotient $R[t,t^{-1}]/(t^n-1)$ is $R[t]/(t^n-1)$, since $t$ there has inverse $t^{n-1}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], the classes $1,t,\ldots,t^{n-1}$ are an $R$-basis; since $g$ maps to zero, all its coefficients vanish. Hence $g=0$ and $f=0$, so $I=0$. This works also for the zero ring and uses no reducedness assumption. Consequently $E=X$ over every affine open of $T$, and therefore $E=X$ globally. Thus $b=e_X$; evaluation on any $S$-scheme gives the required equality $b(a,c)=1$.

The delivery is one commit carrying the item plus the report, with no new nodes. The statement is unchanged. The source (Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Prop. 4.3.1 proof, p.127) has no copy under literature/, so I could not reread that page; I checked the argument on its own instead. Step 1: on a nonempty affine test (so A≠0), character-duality with M=ℤ, L=nℤ says the fppf quotient of G_m by μ_n is D_A(nℤ), and the quotient map is t↦t^n. That quotient is the sheafification of the pointwise quotient. The target is representable, hence a sheaf: fppf coverings are fpqc coverings, and representables satisfy fpqc descent. So the local-surjectivity clause of the sheafification local-bijection lemma gives fppf-local n-th roots. The uniqueness half of the descent lemma lets equality of maps to Z be checked on a cover. Empty and non-affine tests are handled. Step 2 is elementary and correct: b(a,d^n)=b(a,d)^n=b(a^n,d)=b(1,d)=1, so b is trivial on μ_n×G_m. Step 3: the equalizer is the pullback of the diagonal, a closed immersion because Z is separated (Stacks 01QR). Over an affine V=Spec R in the second factor it is cut out by an ideal I of R[t^±1]. μ_{n,V} lies in it, and through Spec Hom this means I⊆(t^n−1). Step 4: R[t^±]/(t^n−1)=R[t]/(t^n−1), which is free on 1,…,t^{n−1} by the monic-quotient node. Taking n above the degree of t^k f forces f=0, for any R including nonreduced ones. I tested R=0, R=F_p[ε]/ε² with f=εt^k, n=1, and p|n. Duplicates: a scan of all node statements found only field-only torsion-density nodes. Cycles: none; the item is not in its 154-node closure.
